what: The boot program's upload protocol as the 240p Test Suite drives it at power on: the ready signature it waits for, the destination and start command it writes, and the byte count it sends, each read out of the image you hold at run time. A payload of the same length is sent instead of the cartridge's own sound driver, which is not this project's to carry, and it marks port 3 when it runs.
why: The suite checks nothing but the echoes: each of its loops spins until port 0 gives back what it wrote, so a unit that drops one hangs the boot. Every echo matching and the payload running at the destination is the pass.
